# Joint capability benchmark (coding / co-work / reasoning) — frozen measurement program

## Execution
`python3 run.py --context PATH --output PATH` measures ONE candidate model on every item declared in
`evaluation.json` and writes `{"protocol_version":1,"items":[...]}` with exactly one row per item.
Items are independent; the program runs at most 2 concurrently (platform per-model request limit) and
persists partial results atomically to `OUTPUT.partial.json` after every item. Completed items present in the
resume context are reused unchanged through `Client.item()`. The SDK is imported from `/workspace/research_sdk.py`
when present, otherwise from the vendored copy in `sdk/`. Only the Python standard library, numpy and scipy are
required by the graders (SciCode steps import numpy/scipy; a few gold steps also declare `math`).

`build_manifest.py` regenerates `evaluation.json` from the same item definitions used by `run.py`
(item ids, weights, question prompts and the three `domain_aggregations`). If `subset.json` exists in the
directory (pilot snapshots only) the item list is restricted to those ids; the final suite has no `subset.json`.

## Item families (145 questions, each independently scored, one scored item per question)
| family | ids | n | domain | weight | output cap | grading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HLE text-only questions | `hle_*` | 44 | reasoning | 1.0 | 16000 tok | upstream HLE system prompt; `Answer:` line extracted; multiple choice compared locally; exact-match answers compared after normalization, otherwise judged by `helper-simulator` with the upstream HLE judge prompt (yes/no) |
| ArXivMath 202606 problems | `arxiv_*` | 16 | reasoning | 2.0 | 24000 tok | upstream prompt (`\boxed{}` final answer); last boxed answer normalized and compared with the gold answer, otherwise `helper-simulator` equivalence judge |
| SciCode (dev split) sub-steps | `scicode_*` | 25 | coding | 1.0 | 16000 tok | candidate implements the step function given the problem context, the gold code of previous steps and the step background; executed in a subprocess against the upstream test cases with targets computed from the gold solution; score 1 only if every test passes (np.allclose rtol 1e-4) |
| LiveCodeBench (release v6, Jan–Apr 2025) hard problems | `lcb_*` | 18 | coding | 1.0 | 20000 tok | code block executed in a subprocess against up to 25 upstream tests (6 s each); score 1 only if all pass; problems with multiple valid outputs were excluded |
| Advanced instruction following | `if01`–`if26` | 26 | co-work | 1.0 | 8000 tok | deterministic programmatic checks (multi-constraint prompts, system-prompt rules, multi-turn histories); score = fraction of checks passed |
| GDPval text-only tasks | `gdpval_*` | 16 | co-work | 1.5 | 16000 tok | candidate writes the deliverable as text; `helper-grader` grades the upstream rubric criteria PASS/FAIL (file-format-only criteria removed, at most 30 criteria kept by score); score = points passed / total points |

Reasoning: 60 items (HLE 44×1 + ArXivMath 16×2), coding: 43 items, co-work: 42 items (IF 26×1 + GDPval 16×1.5).
Each `domain_aggregations` entry is a frozen weighted mean of item scores in [0,1]. The same domain score is used
for every reference benchmark of that domain. No candidate identity or reference label is used anywhere in grading.

## Answer status conventions
Empty candidate text → score 0, `answer_status: missing` (SDK). No parsable final answer (no `Answer:` line, no
`\boxed{}`) → score 0, `answer_status: invalid`. Infrastructure failures are returned as incomplete rows
(`execution_status` ≠ completed) with `score: null`; a helper-judge API failure leaves the item incomplete without
re-asking the candidate. Helper prompts and parsing are in `run.py` (`HLE_JUDGE`, `MATH_JUDGE`, `GDPVAL_JUDGE`).
If the GDPval judge returns an unparsable verdict list, the item is scored from whatever verdicts parsed
(conservatively) and flagged `judge_parse: partial`.

## Provenance
- HLE: bundled fixed-revision text-only release (`resources/hle`, cais/hle 5a81a4c…), stratified random sample
  (seed 20260920) of questions ≤1800 chars with answers ≤60 chars.
- ArXivMath 202606: bundled `tasks.json` (48 problems), 16 chosen by index for short gold answers.
- SciCode: `problems_dev.jsonl` from https://huggingface.co/datasets/SciCode1/SciCode (dev split contains
  gold code; targets computed locally by executing the gold solution, steps whose tests could not be reproduced
  locally or whose targets exceed 300 KB were dropped).
- LiveCodeBench: `test6.jsonl` from https://huggingface.co/datasets/livecodebench/code_generation_lite
  (contest dates 2025-01-04 … 2025-04-06), difficulty `hard`, test payload ≤400 KB, no special-judge problems.
- GDPval: bundled openai/gdpval tasks without reference attachments, prompts not demanding spreadsheet/slide/media
  output, one task per occupation (16 occupations), rubric from `rubric_json`.
- Instruction following: authored for this benchmark (`cowork_if.py`).

## Limitations
- Candidates run at their configured effort; long-thinking models may hit the per-item output caps (truncated
  responses are graded as given, usually 0). This is part of the frozen protocol.
- SciCode/LCB items are single-turn without tool use; repository-level agentic SWE work could not be executed
  in this environment (no container runtime), so coding is measured by scientific programming and algorithmic
  problems, not issue resolution.
- GDPval deliverables are text-only approximations of document tasks; the LLM rubric judge introduces some noise.
- Development measurement covered only a 14-item snapshot per model (time-limited); the full suite was not
  re-measured before freezing.
